## Task 1: Create a Custom S3 Class

```{r}
# Define a constructor for the Circle class
Circle <- function(radius) {
  obj <- list(radius = radius)
  class(obj) <- "Circle"
  return(obj)
}

# Define a print method for Circle class
print.Circle <- function(x, ...) {
  area <- pi * (x$radius ^ 2)
  cat("Type: \"Circle object\"\n")
  cat("Radius:", x$radius, "\n")
  cat("Area:", area, "\n")
}

# Test Task 1
my_circle <- Circle(5)
print(my_circle)
```

## Task 2: Define a Custom Operator

```{r}
# Modify the Circle class to include x and y coordinates
Circle <- function(radius, x = 0, y = 0) {
  obj <- list(radius = radius, x = x, y = y)
  class(obj) <- "Circle"
  return(obj)
}

# Update the print method
print.Circle <- function(x, ...) {
  area <- pi * (x$radius ^ 2)
  cat("Type: \"Circle object\"\n")
  cat("Radius:", x$radius, "\n")
  cat("Center: (", x$x, ",", x$y, ")\n", sep="")
  cat("Area:", area, "\n")
}

# Define the custom operator %>% for checking circle intersection
`%>%` <- function(c1, c2) {
  if (!inherits(c1, "Circle") || !inherits(c2, "Circle")) {
    stop("Both operands must be of class 'Circle'.")
  }

  # Calculate distance between centers
  distance <- sqrt((c2$x - c1$x)^2 + (c2$y - c1$y)^2)

  # Check if circles intersect
  sum_radii <- c1$radius + c2$radius
  return(distance <= sum_radii)
}

# Test Task 2
circle1 <- Circle(radius = 3, x = 0, y = 0)
circle2 <- Circle(radius = 4, x = 5, y = 0)
result <- circle1 %>% circle2
print(result)
```

## Task 3: Write a Function for the Class

```{r}
# Define circumference function
circumference <- function(x) {
  UseMethod("circumference")
}

# Method for Circle class
circumference.Circle <- function(x) {
  return(2 * pi * x$radius)
}

# Test Task 3
my_circle <- Circle(radius = 5)
circ_value <- circumference(my_circle)
print(circ_value)
```

## Task 4: Create a Custom S4 Class

```{r}
# Define S4 class Rectangle
setClass("Rectangle",
  slots = list(
    length = "numeric",
    width = "numeric"
  )
)

# Define constructor function
Rectangle <- function(length, width) {
  new("Rectangle", length = length, width = width)
}

# Define show method for Rectangle
setMethod("show", "Rectangle",
  function(object) {
    area <- object@length * object@width
    cat("Type: \"Rectangle object\"\n")
    cat("Length:", object@length, "\n")
    cat("Width:", object@width, "\n")
    cat("Area:", area, "\n")
  }
)

# Test Task 4
my_rectangle <- Rectangle(length = 4, width = 6)
show(my_rectangle)
```

## Task 5: Define a Custom Operator for the S4 Class

```{r}
# Define the %==% operator for comparing Rectangle areas
`%==%` <- function(r1, r2) {
  if (!inherits(r1, "Rectangle") || !inherits(r2, "Rectangle")) {
    stop("Both operands must be of class 'Rectangle'.")
  }

  area1 <- r1@length * r1@width
  area2 <- r2@length * r2@width

  return(area1 == area2)
}

# Test Task 5
rectangle1 <- Rectangle(length = 4, width = 6)
rectangle2 <- Rectangle(length = 3, width = 8)
result <- rectangle1 %==% rectangle2
print(result)
```
